name: pwm_controller
description: Parameterizable PWM controller with synchronous active-low reset. Counter increments on enabled clock cycles, wraps to zero when it reaches the programmed period, and asserts pwm_out when counter_value is less than duty_cycle.

fixed_assumptions: duty_cycle and period are sampled combinationally from their input ports every cycle.
Counter and pwm_out are registered/synchronous with the rising edge of clk.
When enable is low, counter_value holds its current value.
When period is zero, the counter remains at zero on enabled cycles and pwm_out follows the duty_cycle comparison against zero count.

feature_contracts.description: Asserting active-low reset clears the observable counter and deasserts pwm_out through the reset state.
With reset released and enable asserted, the counter advances on each clock until terminal count behavior is applied.
When the counter reaches the programmed period, the next enabled cycle wraps the counter back to zero.
PWM output is high whenever the registered counter value is strictly less than duty_cycle.
PWM output is low whenever the registered counter value is greater than or equal to duty_cycle.

functionality: Implements a parameterized pulse-width modulation generator using an 8-bit free-running configurable counter. The counter advances by one on each rising edge of clk while enable is asserted. The counter compares against the period input and resets to zero upon reaching the programmed terminal count. The pwm_out output is asserted whenever the current counter_value is less than duty_cycle, producing a duty-controlled waveform with period set by the period input. All state elements clear to zero under active-low reset_n.
responsibilities: Generate a terminal-count wrap based on period.
Produce a combinational PWM compare output from counter_value and duty_cycle.
Provide the current counter value on counter_value for observability and debug.
Support synchronous enable gating and deterministic reset-to-zero behavior.
reset_behavior: When reset_n is low, the internal counter register is cleared to 8'h00 and pwm_out is driven low through the reset state of the compare logic. Upon deassertion of reset_n, counting resumes from zero on the next enabled clock edge.
behavior_rules: On each rising edge of clk, if reset_n is low, clear counter_value to 0.
On each rising edge of clk with reset_n high and enable high, increment the counter by 1 unless the counter is at or beyond period, in which case load 0.
When enable is low and reset_n is high, hold counter_value constant.
pwm_out shall be 1 when counter_value < duty_cycle and 0 otherwise.
counter_value shall always reflect the current registered counter state.
The design must be synthesizable and must not infer latches.
The design must not use asynchronous reset behavior.
The design must not drive any input ports internally.
